A1.justification: Both readable, 11-page PDFs describe the same UniRestore study, with corresponding methods, equations, six figures, and six tables. Neither contains appendix pages; the separately referenced Supplementary Material is absent from both supplied files.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration, classification, segmentation, ablation, and object-detection experiments in Tables 1-6, with qualitative results in Figures 4-6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in Tables 1-6 and Figures 4-6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 retain the same diffusion backbone, CFRM, TFA, losses, training stages, and prompt-based task extension. Figure 2 clarifies the existing modules' placement without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: The restoration datasets, ImageNet/CUB classification, Cityscapes/FoggyCityscapes/ACDC segmentation, and COCO-to-RTTS detection coverage remain unchanged. The changed CUB citation does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain DIP, URIE, NAFNet, PromptIR, DiffBIR, and DiffUIR, including their starred training variants. Table 6 retains the same detection comparators; shortened related-work descriptions do not remove evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The versions retain 15 synthetic degradation types, 80,000/20,000 ImageNet training/test samples, the same evaluation backbones and metrics, and the same baseline training protocols. The detection extension still uses 69,242 COCO training images.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 retains the CFRM/TFA component ablation, four TFA variants, and prompt-only detection extension. Unseen-dataset evaluations and qualitative restoration, activation-map, and segmentation analyses are also retained.

E5.justification: Both supplied PDFs report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-6 match, including UniRestore's 24.32 DIV2K PSNR, 71.65 ImageNet ResNet-50 accuracy, and 58.06 RTTS mAP. Figures 4-6 retain the same qualitative result images and findings.

T1.justification: The feature-dimension definitions, adapter equations, and training-loss formulations in Equations 1-6 are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unifying perceptual and task-oriented restoration, CFRM/TFA effectiveness, and extensibility to additional tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of perceptual/task-oriented trade-offs, joint-training performance declines, cross-task sharing, scalability, and prompt-only extension remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL on the first page, providing an access pointer absent from v1. The implementation, dataset-processing, training, and task-extension details within the supplied PDFs otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 condenses DDP, SFDUnet, and ControlNet discussion while retaining their citations, and removes several super-resolution and ControlNet-variant references. CUB's citation changes to Wah et al.'s dataset report. The retained SRCNN reference is now misplaced in the dehazing citation group; the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 shortens Sections 2.1-2.3, makes small wording edits elsewhere, updates affiliations and equal-contribution information, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 explicitly labels the encoder with CFRM and decoder with TFA, and clarifies their placement in its caption. Figure 3 moves from the left to the right column, with accompanying text reflow. Result tables and qualitative displays retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: Clearer Figure 2 labels and caption, the primary CUB dataset citation, and the new project-page pointer modestly improve comprehension and traceability. Shortened related work loses some detail and introduces the misplaced SRCNN dehazing citation, limiting the benefit. The methods, results, and scientific support remain unchanged.
